searchText: Hi would someone mind explaining me what do ppl mean by when. they say evm. is a stack. based machine , i understand how a stack works but what is its responsibility within the evm ? i initially thought it was part of memory but then the MSTORE and MLOAD opcodes kinda confused me Search the internet for "stack based virtual machine". It is a common term in computer science that broadly describes a particular virtual machine architecture. I know what it is, im just confused to what is its responsibility within a stack based machine <@301186049323958275> It just means that the EVM is a "stack based virtual machine", not a "register based virtual machine" (the two most common types of VMs). More precisely, all computations operate on stack items - not registers or memory. Stack machines can have registers (e.g. JVM, Wasm ...) and register machines can have stacks (e.g. Intel, VAX ...). Even the EVM has two registers - the program counter and the stack pointer.
